literal: Through good conduct they will attain greatness; through misconduct they will attain unprecedented disgrace.
translation: Through right conduct, people attain greatness; through misconduct, they incur unprecedented disgrace.
modern: ஒழுக்கத்தினால் மக்கள் மேன்மையை அடைவார்கள்; ஒழுக்கம் தவறுதலால் அவர்கள் அடையக்கூடாத பெரும் பழியை அடைவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the consequences of good conduct and misconduct. Those who maintain right conduct naturally rise to greatness. Conversely, those who slip into misconduct will suffer disgrace of an unprecedented or unbefitting nature. The repetition of the verb 'எய்துவர்' emphasizes that both outcomes are certain and directly earned by one's own actions. The phrase 'எய்தாப் பழி' highlights that the resulting blame is so severe that it is normally considered unthinkable.
